_comment: UTAH STATE LEGISLATURE — printed name to PolitiDex roster id, 2025 General Session. HUMAN-ACCEPTED. scripts/vr-utah-ingest.mjs proposes this file (--collect, into the cache directory) and reads it (--seed), but never writes it: a vote page prints "Schultz, M." and never a roster id, so every line below is an identification a person made and can be held to. Keys are the EXACT string le.utah.gov prints in a roll-call cell. A printed name that is not a key here is counted, listed in the seed as droppedNotOnRoster, and its vote is DISCARDED — it is never attributed to whoever holds that district today.
_howReviewed: Each proposal was matched on surname plus first-name compatibility within one chamber, then CONFIRMED against the district in the cell's own leglookup link. Every entry below matched its roster district except the six noted in _acceptedWithoutDistrict, whose vote pages carry no link because those members have left the chamber; each of those six was checked by hand against the chamber's own per-year roster (le.utah.gov/asp/roster/roster.asp?year=2025). District was never used as the primary key: a district's occupant changes between sessions, so keying on it would hand a departed member's 2025 votes to their successor.

Gay Lynn Bennion, Utah House district 41 (Cottonwood Heights) 2023–2025. No leglookup link on the 2025 pages — she resigned in Dec 2025 and John Arthur holds the seat. Confirmed against le.utah.gov/asp/roster/roster.asp?year=2025, which lists her at 41, and the surname is unique in the 2025 House.
Jefferson S. Burton, Utah House district 64 (Spanish Fork / Salem) 2023–2026. Same: no link, and Jackie Larson holds the seat since May 2026. The 2025 roster lists him at 64 and the surname is unique in that chamber.
Tyler Clancy, Utah House district 60 (Provo). The 2025 vote pages print no leglookup link for this member because they left the House after the session — now the state homeless coordinator — so no district came off the page. Accepted because the surname is unique in the 2025 House and the roster carries them at district 60.
Matthew H. Gwynn, Utah House district 6 (Box Elder / Weber). Same situation: no link on the page, unique surname in the chamber, roster district 6.
Jefferson Moss, Utah House district 51 (Saratoga Springs / west Lehi) 2023–2025. Resigned Jul 2025; Leah Hansen holds the seat. NOT resolved by surname — 'Moss, C.' is Carol Spackman Moss at district 34 and is a different person — but by printed INITIAL plus the 2025 roster, which lists exactly one Moss, Jefferson, at 51. This is the wave-1 refusal cleared by adding the real person, not by loosening the rule.
Daniel W. Thatcher, Utah Senate district 11 (Eagle Mountain / Tooele) 2023–2025. Resigned Dec 2025; Emily Buss holds the seat. No link on the page; the 2025 roster lists him at 11 and the surname is unique in the Senate.

_printedInitialNotes: Three printed names carry an initial that is not the one a reader would guess from the roster record, and all three are the same harmless thing rather than a mismatch: le.utah.gov prints the member first initial, which for these people is not the name they go by. "Walter, N." is R. Neil Walter, who goes by Neil; "Maloy, A. Cory" is A. Cory Maloy, on the roster as Cory Maloy; "Adams, J. Stuart" is J. Stuart Adams, on the roster as Stuart Adams. Each was confirmed by the district printed beside the name on the vote page, not by the initial, so none of them rests on the coincidence. Recorded here so a future reader checking initials against the roster does not read a bug into a nickname.
_unmappedIsCoverage: `unmapped` below is not an error and not a mystery: it is people who cast recorded votes in this session and are not on the PolitiDex roster at all, whose votes are therefore dropped rather than guessed at. Wave 1 left 26 of 75 representatives and 1 of 29 senators here. Data wave 2 (August 2026) closed all 27 by adding identity-only roster records for the real people, so `unmapped` is now empty for 2025GS. It stays in the file because the next session will refill it.
_refusalsCleared: Wave 1 marked three printed names REFUSED rather than unmapped — 'Moss, J.', 'Peterson, K.' and 'Peterson, T.' — because each shared a surname with a DIFFERENT person already on the roster (Carol Spackman Moss at district 34, Val Peterson at 56) and mapping on a shared surname is how a vote gets handed to a stranger. All three are now mapped, and none of them by relaxing that rule: Jefferson Moss, Karen M. Peterson and Thomas W. Peterson are three distinct people who were simply absent from the roster. With their own records added, the printed initial plus the district on the page resolves each uniquely, which is what a unique human map means. _refusedNames is empty for 2025GS as a result; a future session that produces a genuinely ambiguous name will refill it.
